Posted October 12, 2007 

Analysis by Richard Cowan  


I am happy to be back among old friends at High Times with the launch of a bi-monthly column on HighTimes.com, starting today with Forty Years of Cannabis, which is a bit of personal history to introduce myself to a new generation of HT readers.  

 

When I was National Director of NORML in the early 90s, I often wrote the NORMLizer column for the magazine, but the Marijuana News Report will be my personal perspective on the news. 

 

As I report in the first installment, at the NORML Conference in Los Angeles I am chairing a panel on Saturday morning about Marijuana and the Senior Citizen- Will They Still Arrest You When You Are 64. (Yes, of course they will!) 

 

I am also happy to report that this evening I will be giving an award to my old friend, Mike Gray, the author of Drug Crazy, one of the best books on the insanity of the drug war. 

See 

Exchange Between Mike Gray and the Drug Bizarro On CNN Talkback Live:
Gray Warns That Dutch Will Protest
 

See 

Meanwhile back in what passes as the real world, Al Gore has won the Nobel Peace Prize. 

 

Climate change is off topic for MarijuanaNews.com, and I am as much pro-Polar Bear as any non-seal you are apt to meet, but I am holding my applause. I cannot forget Gore's endless waffling on medical marijuana in his 1990 campaign, and his silence since then.  

See

Gore On Medical Marijuana: "So far there is absolutely no evidence that it has the effect that some people say." Analysis By Richard Cowan   

and 

Even The Washington Post Notices As "Gore Reverses Stance on Medical Marijuana" Getting Worse.  

The problem with being a senior citizen is not so much what you can't remember as what you can't forget.
